# BLO-48402 — refuse GitHub MCP `update_pull_request(draft:false)`; route it to `gh pr ready`

Changed files:

- `src/server/env-guard.ts`: `update_pull_request` joins `GUARD_HOOK_MATCHER`
  and `MCP_GITHUB_WRITE_RE` (so it is lock-gated like the other MCP writes).
  The guard script exits 2 on `mcp__github__update_pull_request` with
  `draft === false`. The message gives the exact `gh pr ready <n> -R o/r`.
- `src/server/env-guard.test.ts`: one test. `draft:false` is refused,
  `draft:true` is allowed, and an edit with no `draft` field is allowed.
  The suite fails if either the refusal or the matcher entry is removed.

Why refuse outright instead of running the hold check here: the BLO-48359
human-hold predicate (latest non-Bot `ConvertToDraftEvent`, human-opened draft,
`HOLD_RE` comment) lives in `scripts/gh-token-wrapper.sh`. A second copy in this
hook would drift. `gh pr ready` runs that predicate, so a Bot-drafted PR still
goes ready in one command. Only the MCP shortcut is closed.

Other GitHub MCP mutations were checked. `create_pull_request` can only create a
draft or a non-draft PR, so it cannot un-draft an existing hold. GitHub refuses
`merge_pull_request` on a draft. The exposed tool set has no GraphQL passthrough.

No upstream change: this is Paperclip-local code under `src/server/`.
